name: tf-lab-four-member-telemetry-authz
description: Meridian Capital trading fabric — telemetry-archive authorization tier, FOUR-MEMBER variant. The 2-node Arista cEOS fabric exports telemetry from dedicated exporter loopbacks — TWO per switch (a primary and a secondary export path) — and the cloud archive tier must authorize writes from EXACTLY the fabric's exporter address range. The exporter addresses are NOT specified here: they are SELECTED by the network design from state harvested off the live devices, and the range the cloud tier must authorize is DERIVED from that selection. Four members make the derivation materially harder than two: with two addresses a free aligned pair almost always exists, whereas four must summarize into ONE prefix that still covers no existing allocation — and the pool's existing allocations are scattered precisely enough that most free-looking selections do not.

nodes.name: telemetry-archive
nodes.authorization: s3:PutObject MUST be restricted to the fabric's telemetry-exporter aggregate — a RUNTIME value produced by the network design (see telemetryExport)

readOnlyDeviceService._whyThisIsHere: The harvest role reaches ceos1/ceos2 ONLY through a self-provisioned read-only MCP service. This document is topology/program reference data and deliberately carries no endpoint/category/tools fields of its own — so the descriptor below is the connection surface, and it must be named in the network pipeline's task description. Omitting it is not a soft failure: the harvest role is correct to refuse to invent connection fields, and the whole leg blocks at Phase 0.
readOnlyDeviceService.lifecycle: Self-provision per the active protocol: register from this descriptor, harvest read-only, then tear down the registration — on approval AND on escalation alike.

telemetryExport.exporterCount: FOUR — two per switch (primary + secondary export path)
telemetryExport.exporterInterfaceConvention: a free Loopback interface per exporter path on each switch
telemetryExport.addressUniqueness: fabric-wide — exporter addresses are advertised /32s, so a duplicate across switches is a real BGP conflict
telemetryExport.existingAllocations: NOT LISTED HERE — the pool already has scattered, asymmetric allocations on both switches. They are discoverable ONLY by harvesting the live devices (interface state and BGP network statements both show them).
telemetryExport.selectedExporterAddresses: RUNTIME — FOUR free /32s, two per switch, SELECTED by the network design from what is actually free at harvest time.
telemetryExport.derivedExporterAggregate: RUNTIME — the smallest single prefix covering ALL FOUR selected addresses, DERIVED by the network design. This is the value the cloud tier must authorize.
telemetryExport._whyFourIsHarderThanTwo: With two addresses, any free aligned pair summarizes tightly and the search space is large. With four, the aggregate must cover all of them AND still cover no existing allocation — and those two requirements interact. A selection made by taking the lowest free addresses one at a time will generally summarize into a prefix that swallows allocations the design was told not to touch. The design must therefore reason about how its selection SUMMARIZES, not merely about which addresses are unused. This file deliberately does NOT state what prefix length results or how the four should be grouped: that is the design's problem to solve and the reviewer's to check, and naming it here would turn the requirement into a target to aim at rather than a property to satisfy.
telemetryExport._whyThisIsUnarguablyRuntime: The objective test: WOULD THIS VALUE CHANGE IF THE RIG WERE REBUILT? Yes — the scatter of existing allocations is re-randomized per build, so the free set changes, so the viable four-member selection changes, so the derived aggregate changes. A value that changes per build CANNOT be pinned in a static design artifact or agreed up front in an interface contract. No Program Architect can know it: the Architect reads only this file and requirements.md and has NO device-state access.

interdependency.chainedValue: the DERIVED exporter aggregate (plus the four selected /32s, for audit)
interdependency.mechanism: the terraform leg's dependencyIds include its own approval gate AND the network sibling pipeline; the context-chainer PIPELINE-predecessor branch chains the network leg's report.md into the terraform leg's §6; the F18 settledness predicate holds the terraform leg until the network deliverable is fully persisted, so it can never design against a half-built address plan.
interdependency.direction_note: network is UPSTREAM by necessity, not preference. This rig's cloud tier is S3-only (aws_s3_bucket.app_logs + random_password.db_master; no VPC/subnet exists), so terraform produces no runtime output the network design would need to match. The program NEVER APPLIES, so no leg can mint a new system-assigned id — every runtime value must derive from EXISTING harvested state.
